audit_result.proof_trace: No `liquidator != borrower` check exists anywhere in the liquidation call chain (`pre_liquidation_check`, `handle_liquidation`, `liquidation_inner`, `ensure_liquidate_borrow_allowed`). The seize formula in `liquidate_calculate_seize_ctokens` (L1050-1060) applies a positive `liquidation_incentive`, making `seized_collateral_value = repaid_debt * (1 + incentive) * (1 - revenue_factor) > repaid_debt` whenever incentive > revenue_factor/(1-revenue_factor), which always holds with typical parameters. Self-liquidation is thus always profitable for the borrower/liquidator. The only deterrent is the `PackageCallerCap` access control requiring admin whitelisting, but this is not an on-chain invariant enforcement.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An operator controlling both a whitelisted `PackageCallerCap` and a borrowing position (or any whitelisted liquidation proxy that does not add its own borrower-check) calls `liquidate()` with their own `obligation_id`; they repay D of debt and receive D*(1+incentive)*(1-revenue_factor) > D of collateral, earning the liquidation incentive at the expense of what external liquidators would otherwise earn, while avoiding the economic penalty of external liquidation.

PROP-01b-partial2-inv-027.text: Self-liquidation must not be profitable: liquidator cannot liquidate own obligation for net gain.
PROP-01b-partial2-inv-027.assertion: forall self_liq(user): value(seized_collateral) - value(repaid_debt) <= 0 for self-liquidation
